clue.text: It'll be done at some stage, to furnish new flats

definitions.text: It'll be done at some stage, to furnish new flats

parts.words: It'll be done at some stage, to furnish new flats
parts.note: flats are painted scenery panels, and a stage is a theatre's platform, so this is work done by stagehands changing the set between scenes

explanation.surface: Something will get done eventually to kit out newly built apartments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At some stage' reads as 'eventually' and 'flats' as apartments; in the theatre a flat is a framed panel of scenery.
explanation.definitionFit: Theatre crews move and replace scenery panels on a stage between scenes, which is exactly the job described.

clue.text: Blocking everyone else's view

parts.note: reads as physically obstructing sight, but means refusing to allow any opinion but one's own

explanation.surface: Standing where nobody else can see.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone conceited about their opinions shuts out others' views, i.e. their opinions.

clue.text: Pop legend lives? That's crazy!

indicators.note: crazy means the letters of the word lives go wild into a new order

explanation.surface: Is the King of rock still alive? That's absurd!
explanation.walkthrough: 'lives' plays on the rumours that the singer is still alive; 'crazy' rearranges it.
explanation.definitionFit: Elvis Presley is a legendary pop and rock singer.

clue.text: Chance for movement from new bowler — two ducks and maiden follow

indicators.note: new means the word bowler appears in a fresh arrangement

parts.note: a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, shaped like O, so two give OO
M is the cricket scoring abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: A new bowler gets a chance, followed by two batsmen out for nothing and a maiden over.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a duck is a score of zero, written O, and a maiden is an over with no runs, M.
explanation.definitionFit: Elbow room is space to move freely, a chance for movement.

clue.text: Can holy order set out to be happy and calm?

indicators.note: the letters are set out in a new order, signalling an anagram

explanation.surface: Can a religious order be laid out to seem content and peaceful?
explanation.walkthrough: 'holy order' looks like a religious community; 'order set out' rearranges CAN HOLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Halcyon days are peaceful, happy times, so the word means serene and joyful.

clue.text: Knowing past planetary investigation

parts.note: fly is British slang for sharp or knowing
by means past, as in going by

explanation.surface: A clued-up previous space probe.
explanation.definitionFit: A spacecraft passing close to a planet to study it is a flyby, a planetary probe mission.

clue.text: Game to exploit a freeze, taking stick for one's goals

definitions.text: Game to exploit a freeze, taking stick for one's goals

parts.words: Game to exploit a freeze, taking stick for one's goals
parts.note: reads as someone willing to take criticism for their aims during a wage freeze, but describes a sport played on frozen water with sticks aiming at goals

explanation.surface: Someone willing to exploit a pay freeze and take flak for their ambitions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Game' looks like 'willing', 'stick' like criticism and 'goals' like aims.
explanation.definitionFit: This sport is played on frozen ice with sticks, aiming to score goals.

clue.text: I'll produce copy detailing society's activities

definitions.text: I'll produce copy detailing society's activities

parts.words: I'll produce copy detailing society's activities
parts.note: copy is journalists' text, and society here is high society, so this is a writer of newspaper tittle-tattle

explanation.surface: A writer promising to report on how a club or society spends its time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'society' suggests an organisation; it means fashionable high society.
explanation.definitionFit: A newspaper journalist who writes about the private lives of celebrities and socialites produces this sort of copy.

clue.text: European has to work very hard to finish early

indicators.note: finishing early means the word stops before its final letter, which is dropped

parts.note: to slave is to toil very hard

explanation.surface: A European worker must put in long hours in order to knock off early.
explanation.definitionFit: A Slav is a member of a people of eastern and central Europe, so a European.

clue.text: Temperate stretch of coast, about fifty miles

indicators.note: about means the coastal word goes around the other letters, enclosing them

parts.note: a bay is an inlet, a stretch of coast
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A mild-weather coastline extends for roughly fifty miles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like 'approximately fifty miles' but tells you BAY goes around L and M.
explanation.definitionFit: Balmy weather is mild and pleasant, a synonym for temperate.

clue.text: A piece of cake — take it thus to avoid stress

definitions.meaning: a piece of cake is something simple, no trouble at all

definitions.text: take it thus to avoid stress
definitions.meaning: the idiom 'take it ...' means relax and not overdo things, so the word fills the gap

explanation.surface: Have a slice of cake and relax so you don't get stressed.
explanation.definitionFit: Something simple is called a piece of cake, and the relaxing idiom fills its blank with this same word.

clue.text: Govt. Department's power covers Eastern cross-country route

parts.note: FO is the Foreign Office, a British government department; with the 's it gives FOS

indicators.note: covers means the word for power wraps around the letter for Eastern

parts.note: sway means power or influence

explanation.surface: A ministry's authority extends over an eastern road across the country.
explanation.walkthrough: FO is the Foreign Office, a UK government department. The Fosse Way is an old Roman road crossing England from Exeter to Lincoln.
explanation.definitionFit: This Roman road runs diagonally across England, a long route through the countryside.

clue.text: I love you — originally smitten somewhere in Somerset

indicators.note: originally means only the opening letter of the word you is used
smitten means struck hard, so the letters are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: A lovestruck declaration from someone smitten at first sight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'smitten' looks like part of the lover's confession but is the anagram signal: ILOVE plus Y, rearranged. Yeovil is a town in Somerset, a county in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Yeovil is a market town in the English county of Somerset.

clue.text: Struggle with Bill's opinions

parts.note: to vie is to compete or struggle
a bill is a narrow headland, as in Portland Bill, and such headlands are points; the 's reads as a plural

explanation.surface: Someone battling against Bill's views.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like a man's name; it is a promontory, so 'Bill's' becomes POINTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Points of view are the stances people take, that is, their opinions.

clue.text: Set I bear with turned up to party

indicators.note: in a down entry turned up means the letters are read from the bottom upwards, reversing them

parts.note: to put is to set or place
Pooh is Winnie-the-Pooh, the famous bear

explanation.surface: I set off with my bear and showed up for the party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' looks like arrived; it reverses PUT I POOH W in this down light.
explanation.definitionFit: To whoop it up is to celebrate noisily, to party.

clue.text: Three-quarters of the team back me up in union contest

definitions.text: Three-quarters of the team back me up in union contest

parts.words: Three-quarters of the team back me up in union contest
parts.note: reads as most of a group supporting a member in a labour union vote, but the speaker is a rugby union player supported by the three-quarters, the back-line players

explanation.surface: A trade unionist boasts that most of the team supports them in a ballot.
explanation.walkthrough: In rugby union the three-quarters are the four backs across the field, who take passes from the scrum-half.
explanation.definitionFit: In rugby union this player feeds the ball from the scrum and is backed up by the three-quarter line.

clue.text: Thrill given to 18. for a start

definitions.meaning: a motorbike engine is started by stamping down on a pedal

explanation.surface: Excitement handed to the entry at 18 to get things going.
explanation.walkthrough: 18 refers to the 18-across answer; the clue's '18.' has a stray full stop from the printing.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting a kick from something means getting a thrill, and a motorbike is started with a stamp of the foot.

clue.text: Returned half of original payment by cheque

indicators.note: returned means the letters picked are sent back, read right to left
half of means the first four of the eight letters of original are taken

explanation.surface: Half of a first payment by cheque came back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half of' takes ORIG from 'original'; 'Returned' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: A giro is a payment made by bank transfer or a cheque-like slip, especially a British state benefit payment.

clue.text: One getting well oiled before joining TT set?

definitions.text: One getting well oiled before joining TT set?

parts.words: One getting well oiled before joining TT set?
parts.note: reads as a drinker getting drunk before meeting friends, but describes a racing machine lubricated before entering the Isle of Man TT races

explanation.surface: A partygoer getting drunk before meeting the teetotal crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Well oiled' suggests drunk and 'TT' teetotal; the TT is the Isle of Man Tourist Trophy, a famous motorbike race.
explanation.definitionFit: Motorbikes are oiled before racing, and the TT is a motorbike race on the Isle of Man.

clue.text: Thanks new clerk as one prepared to take on tasks?

definitions.text: one prepared to take on tasks?

parts.note: ta is British informal for thanks

indicators.note: new means the word clerk appears with its letters in a fresh order

explanation.surface: The boss thanks a fresh office worker for being willing to take things on.
explanation.walkthrough: TA is British slang for thank you. The question mark flags a definition by example: someone who tackles tasks.
explanation.definitionFit: A tackler is someone who tackles things, taking on jobs or opponents.

clue.text: Son's quick finding fault

parts.note: nippy means quick and agile

explanation.surface: A quick son keeps finding fault.
explanation.definitionFit: Snippy means curt and critical, given to fault-finding.

clue.text: Highly effective form of vocal communication

definitions.text: Highly effective form of vocal communication

parts.words: Highly effective form of vocal communication
parts.note: reads as very efficient speech, but highly means high up in the mountains and in high falsetto, as in an Alpine singing call

explanation.surface: A praised, very effective style of spoken communication.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Highly' plays on mountain heights and on high-pitched notes.
explanation.definitionFit: This Alpine singing style switches between chest voice and falsetto and carries across mountain valleys.

clue.text: Turn up twice? Are you serious?

indicators.note: twice means the word for turning up is written two times in a row

parts.note: to come is to arrive or turn up

explanation.surface: Showing up two times? Surely you're joking!
explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation expresses mild disbelief or reproof, like asking whether someone means it.

clue.text: Channel to do some filming for audience

indicators.note: for an audience means the word is heard spoken rather than seen written

parts.note: to shoot is to film a scene

explanation.surface: A TV channel doing a bit of filming for its viewers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Channel' suggests television and 'audience' viewers.
explanation.definitionFit: A chute is a sloping channel down which things slide.

clue.text: Test new version, or retain original one

indicators.note: a new version of the word gives the same letters in a fresh order

explanation.surface: An editor debates trying out a revised draft or keeping the first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new version' rearranges TEST.
explanation.definitionFit: Stet is the proofreader's instruction meaning let the deleted text stand, keeping what was first written.

clue.text: Delivered cards, with a last letter from Greece

indicators.note: with a last means the letter a in the word is moved to the end

parts.note: to deal cards is to deliver them, past tense dealt

explanation.surface: The post brought cards, the final one a letter from Greece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'letter from Greece' sounds like post from abroad, but it is a letter of the Greek alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Delta is the fourth character of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: One can sort of turn back

parts.note: U stands for a U-turn, a sort of turn

indicators.note: back means the word for can is read backwards

parts.note: a tin is a can

explanation.surface: Someone able to perform a kind of reversal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One can' looks like 'a person is able to', but 'can' is TIN, turned round by 'back'.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit is a single thing, one.

clue.text: Regular fluctuation in frequency of arrivals and departures

definitions.text: Regular fluctuation in frequency of arrivals and departures

parts.words: Regular fluctuation in frequency of arrivals and departures
parts.note: reads as a timetable varying, but describes the pitch shift of a sound or light wave as its source approaches and recedes

explanation.surface: A timetable whose arrivals and departures keep varying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arrivals and departures' suggests trains; the physical effect is a change in wave frequency as a source comes and goes.
explanation.definitionFit: This physics phenomenon is the change in observed wave pitch as the source moves towards then away from the listener.
